newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-CHELSEA HELP GULLIT MAKE CUP HISTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-CHELSEA HELP GULLIT MAKE CUP HISTORY.

text.p: Chelsea's Dutch coach Ruud Gullit made English soccer history on Sunday as his side beat Wimbledon 3-0 to reach the F.A. Cup final for the second time in four seasons and the fifth time in their history.

Gullit will become the first overseas coach in the competition's 126-year history to lead his side out at Wembley for the Cup final on May 17 and his side's presence in English soccer's showpiece is testament to his controversial motivational techniques.
This week he revealed his theory that orchestrated and controlled confrontation between him and his players produced a greater team spirit.

And that theory paid off handsomely as two goals from Mark Hughes and one from Italian striker Gianfranco Zola secured Chelsea's place in the final and sent Wimbledon to defeat in a semifinal for the second time this season.
They also lost to Leicester at this stage in the League Cup.

Gullit praised his team and especially Hughes and also spoke of his theory of upsetting his players -- especially Gianluca Vialli, the former Juventus player, who has been kept on the sidelines because of Hughes' outstanding recent form .
"I learnt about this in Holland and in Italy and it worked then, and you can see it worked today. The team all played together and the way they played gave me great pleasure," he said.
"We have no problems here, everything is out on the table. There are 22 players in this team not just 11 and they all took part in today's victory."

A year ago Chelsea lost in the semifinals to Manchester United, but there was never much doubt about them losing this game after Hughes cracked the ball home from close range in the 42nd minute after getting a lucky rebound off Wimbledon defender Alan Kimble's attempted clearance.
"I was pleased with that," said the Welshman afterwards, "I don't score too many from close in and that was an important goal coming just before halftime."
Zola effectively killed off Wimbledon in the 64th minute when he outpaced Dean Blackwell and drove an unstoppable shot past goalkeeper Neil Sullivan from 18 metres.
Zola, who scored Italy's goal when they beat England 1-0 in a World Cup qualifier at Wembley in February, said he had made a promise to himself to return there with Chelsea.
"The atmosphere was so special I said to myself that night, I want to come back here with Chelsea and do the same again. And now I have that chance."

Apart from the opening spell when Wimbledon had more possession and played more aggressively, Joe Kinnear's tired team looked a shadow of the side that put together a run of 19 unbeaten games earlier in the season and Kinnear congratulated Chelsea afterwards.
"They were the better team on the day and they deserved to win," he said.
"Defeat is hard to take, but I hope Chelsea go on and win it, I hope a London club does it."

Wimbledon's attempts at getting back in the game floundered on the Chelsea defence in which Frenchman Franck LeBouef was outstanding. Robbie Earle, who had scored in every previous round, made little impact.

Hughes, who will equal the modern-day record of five Cup final appearance, wrapped the match up in the last minute when he scored his second and Chelsea's third after breaking free of the Wimbledon defence and running on to score with a left-footed shot past Sullivan.
Chelsea have previously reached the final in 1915, 1967, 1970 and 1994 with their only victory coming when they beat Leeds in a replay in 1970.
